quote_zh: NMST (61.2g, 0.278mol), sodium hypochlorite (500ml, 0.745mol) and ruthenium oxide (1.5g, 0.011mol) were charged into a 1L round bottomed flask. This mixture was heated to reflux temperature under stirring for 6-8hours, cooled to 25-30°C and filtered. The filtrate obtained was further cooled to 5-10°C and acidified to pH <3 using concentrated hydrochloric acid(120mL, 1.23mol) to form precipitated product (NMSBA).The product obtained was filtered and dried at 50°C under reduced pressure to obtain NMSBA as light yellow solid. HPLC purity > 95%; Yield: 70%; and Melting point: 210-214°C.
arithmetic_check: Three mass or volume / mole pairs are printed, plus a yield and no product mass. TEST USED, uniform across this run: the MASS-PRECISION INTERVAL. The significant figures of the printed MASS are propagated to a mole interval, and molar_mass_inconsistent is raised only where the printed mole figure falls outside it, so both printed numbers are given the precision they are printed with rather than the mass being treated as exact and only the mole figure's rounding tested. RUTHENIUM OXIDE PASSES: 1.5 g stands for 1.45 to 1.55 g, which against 133.068 g/mol (RuO2, computed with RDKit from O=[Ru]=O) implies [0.01090, 0.01165] mol, and the printed 0.011 mol lies inside that interval. NMST FAILS: 61.2 g stands for 61.15 to 61.25 g, which against 215.230 g/mol (C8H9NO4S, RDKit from the drawn SMILES Cc1ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]) implies [0.28411, 0.28458] mol; the printed 0.278 mol lies OUTSIDE that interval, so the pair cannot be reconciled at the precision the patent prints and this is not a rounding artefact under any reading of either printed number. Read as a molecular weight instead, 61.2 g / 0.278 mol implies 220.14 g/mol against the true 215.230, the printed mole figure being about 2.2% low. molar_mass_inconsistent raised, nothing corrected. Control, described accurately: Example 2 at line 272 prints 5.0 g / 0.023 mol for the same compound and that pair PASSES, its mass standing for 4.95 to 5.05 g and implying [0.02300, 0.02346] mol, which contains the printed 0.023. But it is the only one of the three NMST charges in this patent that passes, and it passes because its deviation is small enough to fall inside the interval its own two-significant-figure mass allows, not because Examples 1 and 3 are clean. All three printed mole figures are LOW against recomputation, and the mass-precision test separates them: Example 1, 61.2 g / 0.278 mol, interval [0.28411, 0.28458], excludes, implied 220.14, 2.2% low, FLAG; Example 2, 5.0 g / 0.023 mol, interval [0.02300, 0.02346], contains, implied 217.39, 1.0% low, no flag; Example 3, 20g / 0.088 mol at line 285, interval [0.09060, 0.09525], excludes, implied 227.27, 5.3% low, FLAG, and Example 3 has raised molar_mass_inconsistent on its own record. Example 3 is the worst case and this section is the middle one. The three implied molecular weights 220.14, 217.39 and 227.27 are not one consistent wrong value, which is the informative part: it points to mole figures computed or rounded imprecisely example by example rather than to one wrong molecular weight propagated across the set, and it is why no single correction would fix all three. All interval bounds, implied weights, true mole values and percentages here are RECOMPUTATION from the printed masses against RDKit molecular weights; the patent prints none of them and none entered a field of the record. NO MASS BALANCE TEST IS POSSIBLE: the patent prints 'Yield: 70%' but no isolated mass for NMSBA, so there is no printed mass to compare against the input moles and no stated pair that disagrees; mass_balance_implausible is therefore NOT raised. For the record, 70% of 0.278 mol at 245.212 g/mol (C8H7NO6S, RDKit) would be 47.7 g, and 70% of the corrected 0.28435 mol would be 48.8 g, but neither figure appears in the document and neither entered the record. NOT MOLECULAR-WEIGHT CHECKABLE: sodium hypochlorite is charged as 500 ml with 0.745 mol (1.49 M, and 0.745 mol x 74.442 g/mol = 55.5 g, i.e. 11.1% w/v if the solution were 500 g, consistent with a commercial hypochlorite solution but with no concentration printed in this Example) and concentrated hydrochloric acid as 120 mL with 1.23 mol (10.25 M, plausible for a 30 to 32% acid); both are solution volumes, not masses of substance, so neither admits a molecular-weight check and neither was flagged. STOICHIOMETRY, computed but NOT written into the record because the patent states no equivalents: hypochlorite 2.68 eq, ruthenium oxide 0.040 eq and hydrochloric acid 4.42 eq on the printed 0.278 mol of NMST. PURITY IS A MEASUREMENT REPORTED AS A BOUND, NOT A SPECIFICATION: the analytical line at 266 prints "HPLC purity > 95%" for the single batch this Example made, so product_purity_pct is 95.0 with purity_method hplc, the inequality kept verbatim in quote_zh, procedure_text and the record notes, and 95.0 understood as that printed lower bound rather than an assayed equality. This agrees with A1, which holds purity_pct 95.0 and raw_text "HPLC purity > 95%" for the same compound. The summary section's "at least 65%" and "at least 85%" are specifications of the invention in general, are not measurements, and are not recorded in any numeric field of this run. "Yield: 70%" is likewise a measurement and is recorded; no isolated product mass is printed, so the yield cannot be cross-checked against a mass.
drawing_evidence: The scheme IMAGE_EXTRACT at line 256, the only such span inside lines 251-267 and the only scheme in the document that a step-(i) section owns directly. p15.json records it as kind 'scheme', between_markers [0046] to [0047], presented_as 'invention_route', with its true printed position between the Example 1 title line and [0047]; build_enriched.py anchored it on the first marker and so emitted it above the EXAMPLES heading. One left-to-right solid arrow, one record. AGREES WITH THE PROSE ON STRUCTURE: reactant C8H9NO4S = NMST of formula (IV), product C8H7NO6S = NMSBA of formula (III), matching the names the prose and the section title give. The enriched span writes the product as CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1 and p15.json writes it as OC(=O)c1ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]; RDKit canonicalises both to CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1, so the two readings of the drawing are the same molecule and the difference is only which end the SMILES starts from. Both match the SMILES A1 carries as aliases. UNDER-SPECIFIES THE PROSE ON REAGENTS: the arrow's only text is 'Oxidant / RuO2', printed above it with nothing below. It names no specific oxidant and does not separate reagent from catalyst, where the prose names sodium hypochlorite as the oxidant and ruthenium oxide as the catalyst with a charge for each; the arrow also shows no acid, no reflux, no temperature and no work-up, where the prose requires concentrated hydrochloric acid to precipitate the product. p15.json's own discrepancies list records both of these. reagent_written_not_drawn raised on that basis. drawing_text_conflict deliberately not raised: nothing drawn contradicts the prose, 'Oxidant' being a superclass of sodium hypochlorite rather than a competing claim, and work-up reagents are drawn nowhere in this document. Route attribution is not in question here, so route_attribution_unclear is not raised: the vision pass set presented_as 'invention_route', and the scheme stands under the EXAMPLES heading drawing step (i) of the invention's own three-step route, not the four-step prior art of US 7,820,863. NMSBC appears nowhere in this section.
